rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice before the appropriate classifier and noun, as in 幾架車 for “a few cars.”

example.english: A few cars are parked at the entrance.
example.jyutping: mun4 hau2 ting4 zo2 gei2 gaa3 ce1

rows.note: Use this when stressing that the number is only a few rather than simply a small number.

example.english: Only a few people are willing to help.
example.jyutping: dak1 gei2 go3 jan4 hang2 bong1 sau2 zaa3

rows.note: Use this for a small minority or small number of people or things, especially in more formal contexts.

example.english: Only a few people oppose this proposal.
example.jyutping: siu2 sou3 jan4 faan2 deoi3 ni1 go3 fong1 on3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice when stressing that only a small number of people or things are involved.

example.english: Only a few people know about this.
example.jyutping: dak1 gei2 go3 jan4 zi1 ni1 gin6 si6 zaa1

rows.note: Use this for a neutral reference to a small number when the stronger sense of “only” is not needed.

example.english: A few people still haven't handed in their homework.
example.jyutping: gei2 go3 jan4 zung6 mei6 gaau1 gung1 fo3

rows.note: Use this when presenting the few as a minority or small group, especially in more formal or abstract contexts.

example.english: A few people opposed this proposal.
example.jyutping: siu2 sou3 jan4 faan2 deoi3 ni1 go3 fong1 on3
